children: rose about 1.6% in the early trading on Friday after Stifel upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $50 from $45, citing growing opportunities in international markets and bags and soft coolers. The shares were on track for a third straight session of gains.
21.3% upside from the stock's last close.
Analyst Peter McGoldrick and team said the company’s Investor Day targets shift the focus away from a recovery in U.S. drinkware toward international markets and newer categories.

new mid-to-high-single-digit revenue growth framework is a step down from its previous high-single-digit to low-double-digit target but called the lower hurdle a “de-risked model.” Even the low end assumes flat U.S. drinkware sales while still delivering high-single-digit EBIT growth and low-double-digit EPS growth.
McGoldrick also highlighted Project Upcycle, a $100 million productivity program split between COGS and operating expenses, saying it supports margin expansion.

The firm estimates FY27 adjusted EPS of $3.42, above the Street estimate of $3.34, and values the shares at 14.6 times its FY27 estimate. It said the company is “compelled by bags and international drivers.”
